title: About Morgan Stanley - An Insider's Experience
description: Morgan Stanley is US based in financial corporation based in New York and through its subsidiaries and affiliates, provides securities products and services to customers, including corporations, governments, financial institutions, and individuals.  Its main areas of business include Global Wealth Management, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management.   In this video, Rishabh of Morgan Stanley talks about how Morgan Stanley was formed,  its prime areas of businesses starting from IPOs to wealth management and what are all technologies involved from Scala to 'Morganised' technologies. Check for internship opportunities in video and advices of Morgan Stanley managers to look while joining any job.     This video is also in one of the series of videos where Rishabh talks about how was the placement procedure of company, different facets of global giant company Morgan Stanley and how it has brought out the best out of him in this work experience of couple of years.

asr.full_text: How is Morgan Stanley's business working? CALL THEM I'm Vishal and I work with Senior Associated Morgan Stanley in M.S. for 2 years. Can you please give us your description of Morgan Stanley? Morgan Stanley is an investment bank based out of India, that out of US. In India it has its offices in Mumbai and Bangalore. I'm talking about the tech offices, I think business offices can be sold at a place. One of the things that I've noticed is there is confusion around J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley. In 1835, there was Glass legal act, which differentiated investment banking from retail banking. Retail banking is the normal banks which we go most like as HDFC Bank, and Bank of Maroondah. And Investment Banks are something special, Investment Bank are usually managing money for a big firm or for a multi-millionaire individual. And they take their assets and they grow it or they try and provide them funds if they require it. So in 1835 in US there was a Glass-Steagall act which said that a single firm cannot do both investment banking and retail banking. And as a result of that, there were two separate individual institutions formed, one was the JP Morgan, and the other was Morgan Stanley. And I think it was later around 1990 or 1995, I'm'm mature on the year but the glasdigal act got removed and since then Margaret Stanley is too tell us what we might see the presence of Morgan Stanley and the ratings I think in India its business is a little limited but from a US perspective I think one of the things that investment banks do is they just help the firms with their IPOs. Now, to explain in layman terms, it could be an apple and a lemon that if you have a firm of, say, 100, whether you want to have it in 10 shares of 10 rupees each, or you want to have 20 shares of 5 rupees each. There are many other basic decisions that are involved in an IPO. So Morgan Stanley has been involved in the IPO. So Morgan Stanley was involved in IPO of many tech firms like Google, Cisco, Netscape, Compact and I think as for Wikipedia and Google's IPO in 2004 were the biggest Internet IPO so far. What are the technologies that Morgan Stanley is working on currently? I think it's basically team-, but we have teams which work on darknet, java, mainframe and there are some teams which work on Python and Scala as well. One of the things that is different in investing in these banks from a pure tech firm is that they do not adopt new technology straight away because of security purposes, so if there is a new open source you will not get to work it on the straight away and of security purposes so if there's any open-source you will not get to work it on straight away and even the existing technology they are so called Morganized wherein Morgan Stanley will build a wrapper around it to make it more secure and then we will use this technology In the database side we are using...we have DB to be our sidebase and there's something which interests me which is called in-memory databases we are using h2nR team with more than 80% systems. So Rishab tell us about the opportunities, the exposure, you get outside of your work life. I think the first thing that comes to mind is trips and to-go outings, these are manager dependent, the better manager you have, the better number of things. I think these are very dependent the moment we do about things from a social activities perspective one thing which I laughed about what was Andy is they have a global volunteering one where it I think the cold from a worldwide will have a lot of volunteering activities available to the class to the employees and it's almost like eight hours of mandatory volunteer work you need to do during that month so that is really good we are also having with some onsite opportunities when I say onsite its actually team dependent but we have basically all the clients in New York right the fellow business counterparts were doing to the business and we are creating the tech for them so there are some opportunities for a team they can very well make use of that and finally we do have something to offer in recruitment wherein I am starting to.. I got the chance to take the first round of phone interviews with many candidates and we get to manage the recruitment tips that we make to our old colleges. So we are not able to do tech interviews at early stages, but we do get to manage the tengo with them for the recruitment process. Are there ways in which Morgan Stanley interacts with students who are currently studying in college. I can't think of anything other than internships right now it could be wrong but to the best of my knowledge I don't think about internships Vishabh, tell us about the work culture and the work environment at Morgan Stanley first thing that comes to mind is the work hard I think the work hards are pretty flexible the firm does not impose anything so basically it's flexible as long as the managers are ok with it you can basically work at any hours that are convenient to you I usually work from say 11 pm to 7 pm or 8 pm you can work any time which suits you Other than that the work pressure I think there is a little bit of work pressure but I don't think that's necessarily a bad thing for me if I'm delivering a business critical functionality, obviously pressure would be there so if a business character needs to go like down x months down the road I'll have to manage my time and need to complete my work within that time and also let the business will excel Right, so actually this thing I learnt from the organ manager Ruby He tells me, whenever I'm looking for a job, I have to look for three things. The type of work I do, the type of people I work with and obviously the money. These are the three basic things which you should actually try to judge other team. The relationship with the manager is pretty open you can voice your opinion as long as you are in the right forum, in the right spirit and the firm will sort of see whatever can be done in that, for that particular request or opinion that you have except for that i'm working in a regular office which is a relatively new office i think the office which i'm trying to write now it started march of 2015 so it's not even a year yet uh we have limited person so what do we have is little limited , compared to some other firms, but we do have some basics like pretty good footwork We have GTV CAL chess And we do have some basic personal fitness, Like yoga and gym and other shifts That's pretty much it
